_why_windows_powershell: ADDED 2026-08-15 after the detector hid J's own interactive PowerShell window twice at 18:03 ET. The ancestry safety gate is NOT buggy -- its premise is. Modern Windows Terminal launches by DCOM activation, so a terminal J opens from the Start menu is spawned by svchost.exe -> services.exe -> wininit.exe with NO explorer.exe anywhere: byte-identical to the service-rooted leak signature. Ancestry therefore cannot distinguish J's terminal from a Task Scheduler leak, and the title allowlist (already honoured for WindowsTerminal.exe) is the intended discriminator. The space matters: automation-spawned shells are titled with a FULL PATH ('C:\WINDOWS\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe' -- 'WindowsPowerShell', no space), so this substring exempts the interactive window WITHOUT exempting them. Verified against the real window-leaks.jsonl records.
